subject: Dedicated performance warranty — metricization, ops gating, and measurement methodology
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finsight.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.s@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed dedicated performance warranty & measurement draft

Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a first-pass term sheet and an accompanying benchmark CSV that shows the baseline runs we used to size the GPU pool. High-level summary:

- Commitment: 48 reserved A100-equivalent GPU-hours (monthly reserved pool) mapped to a 4-node pool with autoscale headroom.
- Throughput warranty: 220k tokens/sec (steady-state aggregate across the pool) with a 95th-percentile per-request latency target of 160ms (token generation path). We propose a measurement window of 30 minutes per verification run.
- Measurement harness: synthetic replay of a representative 48-hour production trace (we used anonymized sample you shared), 10 warmup minutes, 20-minute sampling window, explicit KV-cache cold/warm phases.
- Credits: pro-rated credits if aggregate tokens/sec during verification falls below 90% of target; larger credits/termination rights if <80% after 3 attempts.

Attached: redwood_dedicated_term_sheet_v3.pdf (term sheet with proposed commercial language) and benchmark_results_v1.csv (raw run outputs and plots).

Notes/questions for you:
1) Do you want measurement on tokens/sec (aggregate) or p50/p95 requests/sec bands? We can support both, but billing/credits are simpler using tokens/sec.
2) For latency SLOs — is 95th percentile acceptable, or do you need a P99 gating?

If this aligns, Sean / I can draft the exact clause language for your legal team.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: redwood_dedicated_term_sheet_v3.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB), benchmark_results_v1.csv (csv, 120KB)
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finsight.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Malik <priya.m@finsight.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed dedicated performance warranty & measurement draft

Ben —

Thanks for the doc and the runs. A couple of follow-ups from our infra team (short):

- Tokens/sec vs RPS: Our product shapes requests differently (many short requests, some long). We care about tail latency on short requests (P99) because user experience is sensitive to tails even if aggregate tps is fine. Can you include both tokens/sec (aggregate for billing) and P99 latency measurement for an accepted run?
- Measurement repeatability: we want a deterministic harness we can run in our environment too (to validate). Will you provide the harness and the dataset seed? We also need clear guidance on cache priming so both sides run the same cold/warm phases.
- Noise: cloud noisy-neighbor noise happens — how do you factor out transient host-level noise?

Also, curious about the credit bands. If the pool misses target by 8% in a single run, is that an automatic credit or do you want multiple runs?

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with Sean / Ben to lock the exact knobs.

Cheers,
Alex
Head of Infrastructure, FinSight
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.o@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.s@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-12T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposed dedicated performance warranty & measurement draft — internal negotiation notes

Team — forwarding Alex's response with recommended negotiating posture. Quick points: 

1) Dual-metric approach: agree to measure both aggregate tokens/sec (for billing/credits) and a P99 latency tailgate (for UX gating). Define clear pass thresholds (tokens/sec >= 90% of target => pass; P99 <= 240ms => pass). If tokens/sec >=90% but P99 slightly above, allow ops tuning window rather than immediate credit.

2) Deterministic harness: we can open-source the harness scripts (anonymized) and provide a dockerized runner with seed/state. Insist that verification runs are performed in Redwood-managed verification cluster OR jointly-run in customer's environment with Redwood observers. That addresses noisy-neighbor concerns.

3) Number of attempts: propose up to 3 verification attempts spaced 48 hours apart; if all fail and aggregate <80% => tiered credits (5% credit at 85-90%, 15% credit at 80-85%, contract remedy at <80%).

4) Latency percentile: push back on customer P99 as a billing gate (too sensitive); propose P99 as an operational gating metric used for remediation not automatic credits. Keep tokens/sec as the economic metric.

Please prepare language for Ben to send back to Alex and include a short appendix that explains the harness (warmup/cold phases, seed, concurrency ramp, KV priming).

— Sean
Director, Sales Engineering
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finsight.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.s@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.o@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-14T09:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed dedicated performance warranty & measurement draft

Alex —

Per our internal discussion, please find a succinct negotiated summary below and an appended measurement playbook (excerpt). If this is acceptable we'll convert to contract language and circulate to legal.

Negotiated summary (proposed):
- Pool sizing: 4-node reserved pool (48 A100-eq GPU-hours monthly) with 25% burst headroom for short spikes.
- Economic metric (billing/credits): aggregate tokens/sec measured over the sampling window. Verification target = 220k tokens/sec. Pass threshold = >= 90% (198k tokens/sec).
- Ops gating metric: P99 per-request latency (token path) measured over the same window. Objective = <= 160ms; operational gate <= 240ms. P99 breach triggers remediation window (48 hours) before credits.
- Measurement run details: joint-run harness provided as a docker image + seed files. Run flow: 10m warmup (KV cache warm phase), 20m sampling (steady-state), 10m cool-down. We will supply the harness and random seed ; customer may run locally with Redwood observers.
- Attempts and credits: up to three verification attempts. Single-attempt shortfall 85-90% -> 5% credit; 80-85% -> 15% credit. <80% after 3 attempts -> escalation & remediation clause (possible termination/discount).

Excerpt — Measurement playbook:
1) Dataset: anonymized 48h trace sampled by FinSight (seed provided).
2) Concurrency ramp: linear ramp to target over 4 minutes, hold for warmup.
3) KV priming: explicit 'prime' call that replays top-20% prefixes for 2 minutes pre-warmup.
4) Noise mitigation: run in isolated verification cluster; if run in customer's cloud, collect host-level telemetry and apply median filter across instances to remove one-off host spikes; runs with >15% instance-level variance are quarantined and retried.
5) Reporting: per-run CSV (attached) with per-second tokens/sec, per-request latencies, instance telemetry, and raw stderr logs.

If that looks good I can send updated term sheet with this exact language.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Ben / Sean —

This looks good and addresses our infra team's main concerns. Two small asks before we kick off verification:

1) Please include a short appendix listing the exact p95/p99 measurement code (OpenTelemetry keys) we should expect in the CSV so our engineers can ingest results into our dashboard.
2) Can you add a 24-hour clocking window in the clause that prevents verification runs during our nightly backup windows (we'll provide blackout windows).

Assuming the term sheet is updated with the appendix and blackout window we are ready to sign (I will loop in Procurement/legal next). Can you send a DocuSign version once the doc is updated?

Thanks — appreciate the pragmatic approach.

Alex
Head of Infrastructure, FinSight
